text:
ada (product): quick sync — sales pushed a few picky enterprise asks around archival proof-of-storage and evidentiary chain. two competing proposals: (A) signed manifest + per-object checksums (what we've discussed elsewhere) or (B) append-only Merkle index + RFC3161 timestamping for tamper-evidence. need engineering impact, SOC2/ISO implications, and a rollout plan.

hugo (eng): +1 on exploring Merkle approach. high-level: build an append-only index service that ingests object-level checksums and emits a daily merkle_root; we publish signed roots and optionally timestamp root with RFC3161 TSA for independent attest. Advantages: compact tamper-evidence for long-term archives and cheap verifier path: fetch root + Merkle proof for object. Downsides: extra index storage and a new verification path for customers.

mira (security): from SOC2/ISO standpoint both approaches can work if we meet chain-of-custody requirements. Signed manifest is simpler for immediate rollout. Merkle + TSA gives stronger non-repudiation and is attractive to gov/govcloud customers. Acceptance criteria suggestion: for launch OTP, deliver 3 validated bundles showing either manifest signature OR merkle proof + TSA stamp across BYOK, non-BYOK, and cross-region tenant. If we do Merkle, we must record signer_audit_id and TSA receipt in export metadata.

carmen (legal): legal perspective: independent timestamping (TSA) is compelling — courts often want verifiable timeline. we need language in export evidence that shows when object was attested. also require `legal_hold.jurisdiction` and human-readable `evidence_summary` in all bundles. for retention, legal prefers a 7y cold tier by default but will accept shorter windows if there is a contractual clause. also need an API to request a TSA timestamp on-demand for urgent holds.

noel (ops): ops concerns: TSA calls are external network ops and can fail/queue during incidents. we'd need retry/backoff and an offline fallback (signed merkle root we can publish later with proof-of-delay). index service: shard by tenant and day, retention for index + proofs = 3 years (configurable). storage delta: small (indexes + proofs ~ +1-3%). We'll add `proof.status` metrics and dashboard cards for TSA failures. Canary: 4 tenants for 72h with forced TSA failures to validate fallback.

hugo (eng): sketch of API and storage model:
```
// Append checksum
POST /v1/proofs/{tenant}/append
{ "object_path": "s3://.../obj.gz", "sha256": "...", "ts": "2026-04-01T12:00:00Z" }

// On daily roll
merkle_root = index.compute_root(date=2026-04-01)
publish signed_root = sign(hsm_key, merkle_root)
if tsa_enabled -> tsa_receipt = tsa.timestamp(signed_root)
store {date, merkle_root, signed_root, tsa_receipt}
```
Verifier flow: given object -> fetch proof chain (path->leaf->root), verify sha256, verify Merkle proof against signed_root, verify TSA receipt if present.

mira (security): BYOK nuance: objects encrypted under customer keys still provide the same checksum path but we must include `kms_key_id` + `kms_key_version` in the index entry. If customer won't escrow keys, we still timestamp the merkle_root but we should mark `verification_scope: manifest_only` in metadata and document verification limitations. For acceptance we must validate one BYOK-no-escrow case where security can still verify integrity of encrypted blobs (checksum of ciphertext) but cannot attest plaintext recovery.

carmen (legal): API for on-demand TSA: legal can create a `legal_hold.tsa_request` which triggers an immediate merkle_root publish for the targeted timeframe and returns TSA receipt. we need logs for requester_email and custody_ticket. Add acceptance: legal team must be able to retrieve TSA receipt via `GET /evidence/{export_id}/proofs`.

noel (ops): rollout plan proposal: Phase 1 (beta): signed-manifest only, feature-flag `proofs.merkle_enabled=false` default. Phase 2 (canary): enable Merkle index for subset of tenants with `proofs.merkle_enabled=true` and background TSA calls optional. Phase 3: GA with TSA for gov tenants and on-demand TSA API. Canary cadence: 4 tenants 72h -> 25% traffic 7 days -> full. We'll simulate TSA outages in staging.

hugo (eng): migration note: no backfill of historical archives into merkle index by default (costly). Provide on-demand ingestion API for customers/legal to request backfill for a time window. We'll generate proofs retroactively and produce signed_root + TSA receipt.

ada (product): (typo) ada (product): good thread. decisions we need by next Wed: 1) pick default evidence model for MVP (signed-manifest vs merkle+TSA), 2) TSA on-demand API spec and SLAs (suggest 24h for on-demand stamp), 3) schema fields to add (`merkle_root`, `tsa_receipt`, `proof_version`, `kms_key_id`, `verification_scope`), 4) canary rollout toggles and acceptance tests matrix.

ci-bot: created ticket INF-7300, added canary window and a staged test matrix entry for TSA-failure simulation.

hugo (eng): my recommendation: ship signed-manifest MVP this sprint and Merkle+TSA as a follow-up targeted at gov/BYO-heavy customers. we can implement index service in parallel.

mira (security): agree with staged approach. security will prepare automated verification harness for both flows.

carmen (legal): legal OK with staged approach as long as we expose on-demand TSA and keep documented limitations.

ada (product): thanks everyone — i'll write the RFC with acceptance checklist and feature flags. will tag eng/ops/security for final sign-off. :white_check_mark:
